A common approach is to use a pre-trained convolutional network such as ResNet-18 to obtain compact, expressive feature representations from each incoming frame. An online active learning module then evaluates these deep features to decide which images are most informative to annotate. This setup decouples heavy feature extraction from lightweight querying logic, making it suitable for high-throughput production environments. By selectively labeling only critical frames, the system maintains accurate process monitoring while significantly limiting manual annotation effort.

canonical_topics.name: Gradient Embedding Diversity Sampling for Deep Streams
canonical_topics.description: In deep streaming active learning, each incoming instance can be represented by the gradient of the loss with respect to the final network layer, using the model’s current prediction as a pseudo-label. These gradient vectors act as embeddings that capture how each example would update the model if it were labeled. A determinant-based selection rule, often implemented via a covariance matrix over gradient embeddings, chooses points that jointly maximize diversity and information gain. This results in querying examples that cover different directions in gradient space instead of repeatedly selecting similar uncertain instances. The approach is particularly well-suited to mini-batch or continual training regimes where deep models are updated incrementally.

canonical_topics.name: Slice-Aware Active Label Budgeting for Streaming Object Detection
canonical_topics.description: Streaming object detection in domains such as autonomous driving must contend with highly imbalanced conditions, including rare but safety-critical scenarios like fog, heavy rain, or nighttime. Slice-aware active learning addresses this by partitioning the data stream into slices corresponding to different conditions and tracking model performance per slice. Instead of allocating labels proportionally to slice frequency, the method dynamically directs more of the annotation budget to slices where the detector underperforms. This counters the tendency of passive or frequency-based sampling to neglect rare yet important environments. In deep detection pipelines, such slice-aware budgeting helps maintain robust performance across diverse conditions while keeping overall labeling costs under control.

topics.title: Real-time label availability in streams
topics.description: The section assumes that queried data points from a stream receive labels immediately. This real-time label availability is treated as a foundational condition for many active learning methods in streaming settings. It directly influences how quickly the model can adapt to incoming data and support subsequent querying decisions.

topics.title: Implementation challenges and annotation tools
topics.description: Despite its advantages, real-time annotation introduces practical implementation challenges, such as coordinating timely human or system responses and integrating them seamlessly into the learning pipeline. The section notes that these issues need to be addressed through advanced data annotation tools, which can support efficient labeling workflows in streaming environments.

topics.title: Batch-mode active learning with streamed sampling
topics.description: This topic addresses training deep neural networks from data streams under memory constraints, where instances are sampled in real time but labels and model updates are deferred until a batch is formed. The approach combines streaming data acquisition with batch-mode active learning, in which queried instances are accumulated and then labeled and used for model updates in batches. This design balances computational and memory limitations with the need for timely sampling decisions in streaming environments.

topics.title: Active learning on data streams
topics.description: The section emphasizes the specific challenge of performing active learning when data arrive as a continuous stream and decisions must be made in real-time. Methods must select the most informative data points on-the-fly, under constraints such as limited labeling budgets and evolving data distributions. This contrasts with pool-based active learning where the full dataset is available in advance.

topics.title: Nonlinear regression and Bayesian optimization
topics.description: A key future direction is to develop online active learning strategies tailored to regression models, especially beyond linear models and linear bandits. The section notes growing interest in using Bayesian optimization techniques for active learning in nonlinear regression problems, where the goal is to select query points that improve function estimates efficiently. These methods can exploit probabilistic surrogate models to balance exploration and exploitation in streaming contexts.

topics.title: Object detection in data stream AL
topics.description: Object detection appears as a specialized task within online active learning for data streams, treated with single-model strategies. Both stationary and batch-processed settings are represented, suggesting interest in selectively labeling complex structured outputs (e.g., bounding boxes) under streaming constraints. This indicates an extension of AL for streams beyond standard classification and regression to more complex computer vision tasks.

topics.title: Limits of ensemble and batch online methods
topics.description: This topic highlights that ensemble models and batch-based approaches, although dominant in online classification, rely on assumptions that may break in real-world streaming applications. When data arrive continuously and resources are constrained, forming batches or maintaining multiple models may be infeasible. This motivates investigation into alternative online learning and sampling paradigms better suited to strict temporal or memory budgets.

topics.title: Query strategies for online active learning
topics.description: The survey reviews strategies for selecting the most informative data points in an online setting, where instances arrive sequentially. Key query mechanisms include uncertainty sampling, diversity sampling, query by committee, and reinforcement learning-based approaches. These methods aim to optimize which instances are labeled under limited annotation budgets while the data stream evolves. The topic concerns query selection criteria, model informativeness measures, and sequential decision-making policies.

canonical_topics.name: Online Active Learning on Data Streams
canonical_topics.description: This topic covers active learning when data arrive as a continuous stream and querying decisions must be made in real time. It emphasizes the common assumption that queried instances receive labels immediately, enabling rapid model adaptation and iterative selection. The dependence on real-time label availability shapes which algorithms are feasible in practice and how quickly models can react to evolving data distributions. It also highlights the need for practical annotation workflows and tools that can deliver timely labels and integrate seamlessly into streaming learning pipelines.

canonical_topics.name: Query Strategies and Constraints in Online Active Learning
canonical_topics.description: This topic focuses on strategies for selecting informative instances in online active learning, where data arrive sequentially and labeling budgets are limited. It includes mechanisms such as uncertainty sampling, diversity-based selection, query-by-committee, and reinforcement-learning-driven policies tailored to streaming data. The discussion also highlights that many dominant online classification approaches rely on ensembles or batch formation, which may be infeasible under tight memory, latency, or computational constraints. These limitations motivate the development of new, lightweight querying and modeling paradigms that better align with real-world streaming scenarios.

canonical_topics.name: Batch-Mode Active Learning with Streamed Sampling
canonical_topics.description: This topic addresses learning from data streams when instances are observed online but labels and model updates are deferred and processed in batches. Streamed sampling policies decide in real time which instances to store and later query, while respecting strict memory constraints. Once a batch is formed, the selected instances are labeled and used to update deep models in a standard batch-mode fashion. This hybrid design seeks to balance the responsiveness of streaming acquisition with the computational efficiency and stability of batch training.

canonical_topics.name: Online Active Learning for Nonlinear Regression
canonical_topics.description: This topic explores active learning methods for regression in online or streaming settings, with a particular emphasis on nonlinear models. It highlights the role of Bayesian optimization and related techniques that use probabilistic surrogate models to guide query selection. By balancing exploration and exploitation, these methods aim to efficiently improve function estimates while new data arrive over time. The focus is on extending beyond linear models and bandit formulations to richer nonlinear regression scenarios in dynamic environments.

canonical_topics.name: Streaming Active Learning for Object Detection
canonical_topics.description: This topic considers object detection as a structured prediction task within online active learning for data streams. It examines how to selectively label complex outputs such as bounding boxes under constraints on annotation cost and latency. Both single-model, fully online settings and scenarios with mini-batch processing are discussed. The goal is to extend data-stream active learning beyond classification and regression to more complex computer vision tasks while respecting streaming and resource constraints.
